tasks.answer: The flight delay compensation batch workspace is FlightDelayCompensationBatchScreen (catalog ID flight-delay.FlightDelayCompensationBatchScreen, export FlightDelayCompensationBatchScreen), imported from '@/features/flight-delay-compensation/batch-detail-screen'. The only required prop is batchId. Its constraint notes that it also needs query, auth and router providers and handles offline/conflict states.

The catalog contains no dedicated 'special passenger booking list' variant; the only matching booking-list component is the generic TravelerBookingListScreen (catalog ID bookings.TravelerBookingListScreen), imported from '@/features/traveler-bookings/booking-list-screen'. Its required prop is navigate; initialStatus is optional. It is a paginated traveler booking list with search and filters, and queries/actions are permission-gated, so special-passenger results are expected to be reached through its filters rather than a separate specialized screen.

The password input is auth.PasswordInput (export PasswordInput), imported from '@/features/auth/password-input'. It has no required props. Errors are shown as a string by the surrounding UiFormField wrapper: the component must be used inside UiFormField, and it exposes show/hide labels plus the form-field error supplied by that field wrapper rather than rendering validation errors itself.

The mobile booking list uses business.SearchBar and business.FilterSheet, both imported from '@/components/business/mobile'. SearchBar is the mobile search bar with an optional onFilter action (required props: value, placeholder, onChange). FilterSheet is the bottom filter sheet with reset/confirm actions (required props: visible, title, children, onClose; onConfirm runs before the sheet closes).

components.note: onFilter is optional and adds the filter icon button.
onConfirm is optional and runs before the sheet closes.

tasks.answer: The global auth recovery dialog is common.AuthRecoveryDialog (export AuthRecoveryDialog), imported from '@/components/common/auth-recovery-dialog'. It takes no required props and is mounted once near the app root; it subscribes to the auth recovery store, lazily renders its view, and renders null while no recovery event is pending. The view itself is the separate common.AuthRecoveryDialogView (required prop: detail).

notes: One search per task with --limit 5 --details; search results were sufficient, so no get calls were made. No config, source, or component-catalog.json files were read. Task 2 returned only the generic traveler booking list; no dedicated special-passenger variant surfaced, so that absence is reported with medium confidence. Task 4's two components are also broken out in the extra 'components' array.
